title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: u : A -> A' is a homomorphism of abelian varieties of dimensions n <= n' with finite kernel, for example the inclusion of an abelian subvariety. The page computes the Gysin map u_* in l-adic cohomology. Write T(A) = T_{Q_l}(A) for the rational Tate module.

(1) Restriction. Pullback gives a surjection H^1(A') -> H^1(A) -> 0. Its kernel K has rank 2(n'-n). Since H^* = Lambda^* H^1 for abelian varieties, the top exterior powers factor:
Lambda^{2n'} H^1(A') ~ Lambda^{2n} H^1(A) (x) Lambda^{2(n'-n)} K.
Here Lambda^{2n'} H^1(A') = H^{2n'}(A') and Lambda^{2n} H^1(A) = H^{2n}(A).

(2) Normalisation. The class u_*(1_A) lies in the line Lambda^{2(n'-n)} K(n'-n) inside H^{2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n). This is the cycle class of u(A) times the degree; it is the decomposable vector attached to the subspace K. It is normalised by the following rule. Take the characteristic (orientation) class of H^{2n}(A)(n) times u_*(1_A); this equals d times the characteristic class of H^{2n'}(A')(n'). The integer d is read off from the Z_l-lattices, via the cokernel (index/torsion) of T_{Z_l}(A) -> T_{Z_l}(A'). The first line ('nulle sur ..., à un scalaire près') seems to end a preceding characterisation of the class, which is unique up to a scalar.

(3) Poincaré duality. The cup product H^i(A) x H^{2n-i}(A) -> H^{2n}(A) ~ Q_l(-n) is perfect. Hence
H^i(A) ~ H^{2n-i}(A)^vee(-n) ~ Lambda^{2n-i} T(A)(-n).

(4) Conclusion. u_* : H^i(A) -> H^{i+2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n) becomes the map
Lambda^{2n-i} T(A)(-n) -> Lambda^{2n-i} T(A')(-n),
and it equals Lambda^{2n-i}(u_1) (x) Q_l(-n), where u_1 = T(u). The degrees match:
H^{i+2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n) ~ Lambda^{2n-i} T(A')(-n).
This is the transpose of the statement that u^* = Lambda^{2n-i}(u_1^vee), which is the content of the normalisation in (2).

Purpose: this gives explicit linear-algebra descriptions of correspondences and Gysin maps on abelian varieties. It belongs to the program of verifying the standard conjectures (Lefschetz/Künneth-type statements) and the Tate/Hodge conjectures for abelian varieties via Tate modules.
errors: If u is the inclusion of an abelian subvariety, coker(T_{Z_l}(A) -> T_{Z_l}(A')) is torsion-free. The 'd' then only becomes nontrivial for homomorphisms with finite kernel, where d = deg(A -> u(A)). Even then the cokernel only detects the l-primary part of d. The N.B. identifying d via the Z_l Tate modules is therefore at best correct up to l-adic units, a gap that would matter only for integral statements.
The notation H^1(A'^*) is ambiguous (dual abelian variety or a typo for A'). The argument as written only makes sense with H^1(A').

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine computation of Gysin maps for homomorphisms of abelian varieties in terms of exterior powers of Tate modules. This is standard material used in the 1968 work on standard conjectures for abelian varieties; nothing new beyond the normalisation bookkeeping with the degree d.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'nulle sur Q_l(A) (en gros: la condition à un scalaire près) et tel que, si'.
'-K- H^1(A'*) -> H^1(A) -> 0' should be read as 0 -> K -> H^1(A') -> H^1(A) -> 0. The star on A' is unclear and may be a stray mark.
'N.B. d est aussi le conoyau' is probably 'd est aussi l'ordre (indice) du conoyau de T_{Z_l}(A) dans T_{Z_l}(A')'.
In the final line, the target reads H^{i+2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n); the '2(n'-n)' is overwritten in the manuscript.
